36.0.s.en: 1. Sennacherib seizes the cities of Judah:

36.0.0.en: "Now it came to pass in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, that Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the defenced cities of Judah, and took them." [1].

36.0.1.en: The invasion of Judah by Sennacherib is recorded here in (Isa 36) and also in (2 Kgs 18:13-20), and by comparing the two texts the following is observed:

36.0.2.en: a. It is stated in (2 Kgs 18) that Hezekiah sent to the king of Assyria apologizing to him and saying: "I have offended; return from me: that which thou puttest on me will I bear," and indeed he imposed on him a tribute of three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold, which Hezekiah paid out of the house of the LORD and out of the treasures of the king's house... But Sennacherib broke the covenant and again sent an army to storm Jerusalem. The history of Assyria confirms this, for Hezekiah is counted as a bird in a cage who was unable to go out of Jerusalem, and that he paid the tribute, and that 200,000 persons of his people fell captive.

36.0.3.en: The prophet Isaiah did not mention the matter of the tribute, because he did not aim at the history of the life of Hezekiah, but wanted to bring out God's dealings with him, to confirm God's ability to save when the matter seems impossible.

36.0.4.en: b. Some scholars see that Sennacherib made two campaigns of invasion against Judah, the first in 701 B.C. and the other in 688 B.C., in the days of Tirhakah king of Egypt and Cush (Isa 37:9).

36.0.5.en: c. It is stated in (2 Kgs 18:17) that Sennacherib sent with Rabshakeh two commanders, Tartan and Rabsaris; the mission included three commanders, and Rabshakeh was the only speaker among them.

36.0.6.en: Some see that Rabshakeh is not the name of a person but a title equivalent to "chief cupbearer," who tastes the wine before the king drinks of it so that the king may not be poisoned, and who also performed other principal roles in the royal palace.

36.0.7.en: God allowed this distress in the days of Hezekiah, who carried out many reforms among the people, although many, especially among the religious and civil leaders, cared for outward reform without the inward, so they cared for formalities without the holy life. God wanted to prove Hezekiah and turn the distress into His glorification. On the other hand, He wanted to reveal Hezekiah's weakness to himself, for his courage failed him and his reliance on God was not complete... By trial he confessed his weakness, and his faith in God and his trust in Him increased.

36.1.s.en: 2. His sending of Rabshakeh to Jerusalem:

36.1.0.en: 2 And the king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem unto king Hezekiah with a great army. And he stood by the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller's field. 3 Then came forth unto him Eliakim, Hilkiah's son, who was over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, Asaph's son, the recorder. 4 And Rabshakeh said unto them, "Say ye now to Hezekiah, Thus saith the great king, the king of Assyria, What confidence is this wherein thou trustest? 5 I say, mere words of the lips are counsel and strength for war. Now on whom dost thou trust, that thou rebellest against me? 6 Lo, thou trustest in the staff of this broken reed, on Egypt; whereon if a man lean, it will go into his hand, and pierce it: so is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all that trust in him. 7 But if thou say to me, We trust in the LORD our God: is it not he, whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah hath taken away, and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, Ye shall worship before this altar? 8 Now therefore give pledges, I pray thee, to my master the king of Assyria, and I will give thee two thousand horses, if thou be able on thy part to set riders upon them. 9 How then wilt thou turn away the face of one captain of the least of my master's servants, and put thy trust on Egypt for chariots and for horsemen? 10 And am I now come up without the LORD against this land to destroy it? The LORD said unto me, Go up against this land, and destroy it."

36.1.1.en: Sennacherib sent Rabshakeh from Lachish (Lakhish), a fortified city lying in the plains of Judah (Josh 15:33, 39), formerly known as Tell el-Hesi, which is 16 miles northeast of Gaza and eleven miles southwest of the city of Jibrin; it is now thought more likely to lie at Tell ed-Duweir, five miles southwest of Beit Jibrin. Sennacherib besieged it, and from the camp in front of it he sent Rabshakeh to Jerusalem so that the king and his men might surrender it.

36.1.2.en: Rabshakeh stood with a great army by the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller's field [2], that is, the field of the bleacher of cloth, outside Jerusalem and very near it, where those on the wall of the city could hear whoever spoke in the fuller's field. Some think it was in the Kidron Valley, and that the conduit referred to is the tunnel connecting the Virgin's Spring with the Pool of Siloam, although others see that it was north of the city, since the north was the natural side from which attack came.

36.1.3.en: Eliakim, who succeeded Shebna, came out to him, being in charge of the king's house (Isa 22:15-20), something like the head of the ministry; and Shebna the scribe, who records for the king the most important events as a reminder and plays the role of historian of the king's life; and also Joah the recorder.

36.2.0.en: Rabshakeh mocked King Hezekiah before his great men, for he called Sennacherib "the great king, the king of Assyria," while he gave no title to Hezekiah [4]. He derided him because he trusted in Pharaoh of Egypt, saying: "Lo, thou trustest in the staff of this broken reed, on Egypt; whereon if a man lean, it will go into his hand, and pierce it" [6]. In this he spoke the truth, that whoever trusts in an arm of flesh leans on a broken reed that cannot support him but even pierces his hand. He also mocked him because he trusted in God his God, saying: "Is it not he, whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah hath taken away, and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, Ye shall worship before this altar?... Neither let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD, saying, The LORD will surely deliver us: this city shall not be delivered into the hand of the king of Assyria... Hath any of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?... Who are they among all the gods of these lands, that have delivered their land out of my hand, that the LORD should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?" [7, 15, 20].

36.2.1.en: In the very same place where Ahaz mocked the Lord, refusing to deal with God and relying on the human arm (Isa 7), Rabshakeh came to mock God, as though the sons of Judah were drinking from the cup that Ahaz their king had offered them before! In the very same place where Isaiah came to Ahaz asking him to ask a sign of the Lord to confirm God's ability to save, and he refused, Rabshakeh came to mock Judah and their king and their God!

36.3.0.en: Hezekiah also had relied on human treaties with Pharaoh, and God rebuked him for it on the tongue of a pagan man, calling them mere words of the lips, verbal counsel [5] that has no power or effectiveness. Now he wagers with him that he will give him two thousand horses if he brings two thousand horsemen from his people able to use them. It is as though he were saying to him: Why do you rely on the horses of Egypt and its horsemen? Here we offer you the horses; offer us your men!

36.4.0.en: 11 Then said Eliakim and Shebna and Joah unto Rabshakeh, "Speak, I pray thee, unto thy servants in the Aramaic language; for we understand it: and speak not to us in the Jews' language, in the ears of the people that are on the wall." 12 But Rabshakeh said, "Hath my master sent me to thy master and to thee to speak these words? hath he not sent me to the men that sit upon the wall, that they may eat their own dung, and drink their own piss with you?" 13 Then Rabshakeh stood, and cried with a loud voice in the Jews' language, and said, "Hear ye the words of the great king, the king of Assyria. 14 Thus saith the king, Let not Hezekiah deceive you: for he shall not be able to deliver you. 15 Neither let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD, saying, The LORD will surely deliver us: this city shall not be delivered into the hand of the king of Assyria. 16 Hearken not to Hezekiah: for thus saith the king of Assyria, Make peace with me, and come out to me: and eat ye every one of his vine, and every one of his fig tree, and drink ye every one the waters of his own cistern; 17 Until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of corn and wine, a land of bread and vineyards. 18 Beware lest Hezekiah persuade you, saying, The LORD will deliver us. Hath any of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria? 19 Where are the gods of Hamath and Arphad? where are the gods of Sepharvaim? and have they delivered Samaria out of my hand? 20 Who are they among all the gods of these lands, that have delivered their land out of my hand, that the LORD should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?" 21 But they held their peace, and answered not a word: for the king's commandment was, saying, "Answer him not."

36.4.1.en: Since Rabshakeh used a war of nerves to stir up the people against the king and his men, and to drive them to despair and destroy their faith in the saving God, Hezekiah's men asked Rabshakeh to speak in Aramaic, the Syriac, which was spoken by the inhabitants of the north and east of Palestine and was understood by the Assyrians since it belongs to the same family as their languages, and which the common people of the Jews did not understand. But Rabshakeh insisted on speaking in Hebrew, to stir up the people and cause a kind of division, hoping he might ignite a civil war among the people and the leaders.

36.4.2.en: This is the work of the enemy of good: he uses the language that stirs up our weakness, and that causes division and splits.

36.4.3.en: Rabshakeh wanted to stir up the people, so he reminded them of the destruction that would come upon them instead of their enjoying the good things in Assyria, to show that Hezekiah was deceiving them and that their God would not deliver them. He uses the same method that the enemy of good has used through all generations, for today we see the followers of the "Church of Satan" in America proclaiming that they worship him because he answers them and gives them their requests, which God does not give them.

36.4.4.en: The principal work of the enemy of good is to stir up terror in a person's life and to make him doubt the power of faith. On one side he crushes their spirit with intimidation and terror, and on the other side he wants to isolate them from God, their King and Savior, so as to have them to himself. Therefore the prophet David cries out, saying: "Many there be which say of my soul, There is no help for him in God" (Ps 3:2); "All they that see me laugh me to scorn: they shoot out the lip, they shake the head, saying, He trusted on the LORD that he would deliver him: let him deliver him, seeing he delighted in him" (Ps 22:7-8); "For mine enemies speak against me; and they that lay wait for my soul take counsel together, saying, God hath forsaken him: persecute and take him; for there is none to deliver him" (Ps 71:10-11). This is the picture of the war of the enemy of good, who mocks the believers and insults them, crushing their souls until they lose their hope in the Lord their God, so that he may overtake them and bring them down with him to the pit. The enemy wanted to practice the same war on the Representative of mankind and their Savior, for it was said to Him: "He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him" (Mt 27:42).

36.5.0.en: "But they held their peace, and answered not a word: for the king's commandment was, saying, Answer him not" [21] (2 Kgs 18:36). It was expected that they would declare their revolt and rebellion against the king, but they kept silent as a sign of obedience and trust, awaiting the king's command and instructions. They obeyed the king who asked them not to answer him, that is, not to enter into dialogue with him lest they fall into weakness as Eve fell by her dialogue with the old serpent. As St. John Chrysostom says: [She ought to have kept silent; she needed not to exchange talk with him, but in foolishness she disclosed the Master's saying, and so gave Satan a great opportunity... See what an evil this is, to deliver ourselves into the hands of our enemies and of those who plot against us]. He also says: [Since Satan was not able to offer anything in practice, he offered rather promises in words. Such is the character of deceivers]. And St. Augustine says: [God is our Leader and Satan is our destroyer; the Leader presents His commandment, while the destroyer suggests a deception. Shall we listen to the commandment or to the deception?!].

36.6.0.en: 22 Then came Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah, that was over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph, the recorder, to Hezekiah with their clothes rent, and told him the words of Rabshakeh.

36.6.1.en: The men came to Hezekiah with their clothes rent and told him the words of Rabshakeh [22]... they came in sorrow and bitterness to the king.

36.6.2.en: Would that we too, when we feel bitterness, would not rend our garments but rend our hearts with repentance, taking refuge in Christ the King, who alone is able to give us good counsel and who works in us by His Holy Spirit.

37.0.s.en: 1. Hezekiah takes refuge in God and in His prophet:

37.0.0.en: 1 And it came to pass, when king Hezekiah heard it, that he rent his clothes, and covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD. 2 And he sent Eliakim, who was over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests covered with sackcloth, unto Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz. 3 And they said unto him, "Thus saith Hezekiah, This day is a day of trouble, and of chastening, and of insult: for the unborn children are come to the birth, and there is not strength to bring forth. 4 It may be the LORD thy God will hear the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria his master hath sent to reproach the living God, and will reprove the words which the LORD thy God hath heard: wherefore lift up thy prayer for the remnant that is left."

37.1.0.en: Opinions differ about the assessment of Hezekiah's conduct. Some saw in him the pious, devout and humble man, who therefore wrested God's mercies, although afterward he fell into pride and perished; and some see that what Hezekiah did was not from devotion or from faith, because shortly afterward he gave the treasures of the temple to Sennacherib (2 Kgs 18:14-16) and said to him, "I have offended." Terror and fear also overtook the king, and in his speech he repeated the phrase "the LORD thy God" [4], and not "the LORD our God" or "my God."

37.1.1.en: We return to the king to see him, on hearing the words of Rabshakeh, "rent his clothes, and covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD" [1]. That was a sign of his sorrow together with his humbling before God.

37.1.2.en: Hezekiah sent Eliakim and Shebna and the elders of the priests covered with sackcloth to Isaiah the prophet [2]. The situation had changed: whereas the civil and religious leaders had mocked Isaiah when he went barefoot and naked warning them that Pharaoh and his men would not be able to rescue them (Isa 21), now here they come to him wearing sackcloth in bitterness, declaring their need of his prayers and his counsel. They realized that it was "a day of trouble, and of chastening, and of insult" [3], so let it be a day of repentance and prayer. They felt "that the unborn children are come to the birth, and there is not strength to bring forth" [3]; who can help but God through prayer?! Pharaoh with all his resources cannot give a pregnant woman strength to give birth even when the time of labor has come... Prayer is the "midwife" of mercy that brings about the birth.

37.1.3.en: St. John Chrysostom says: [Nothing equals prayer! It makes the impossible possible, and the difficult easy. A man who prays cannot fall into sin]. And Fr. Theophan the Recluse says: [Prayer is everything; it is the summary of everything: faith, life according to faith, salvation, etc...] He also says that prayer is [the breath of the spirit], it is [the measure of the spiritual life], and the whole Church [breathes through prayer].

37.1.4.en: Rabshakeh exalted himself and reproached the living God, therefore the matter requires the intervention of this God to declare His glory and His power, and for the salvation of the remnant faithful to Him. The psalmist says: "O God, how long shall the adversary reproach?" (Ps 74:10).

37.2.0.en: 5 So the servants of king Hezekiah came to Isaiah. 6 And Isaiah said unto them, "Thus shall ye say unto your master, Thus saith the LORD, Be not afraid of the words that thou hast heard, wherewith the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me. 7 Behold, I will put a spirit in him, and he shall hear tidings, and return to his own land; and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land."

37.3.0.en: Isaiah mocked the king of Assyria and his men, for he counted his men of war and his commanders as boys, having neither understanding nor power; so it is not fitting for Hezekiah to fear them [6].

37.4.0.en: What Sennacherib did through his men is done to him; for his men tried to fill the ears of the people with words of blasphemy and also threatened them with death, therefore the ears of the king of Assyria were filled with news that troubles him [7] and he falls by the sword in his land. He uttered harsh words and threatened death, so the words rebounded upon him and he was killed. As for His saying, "Behold, I will put a spirit in him" [7], it means that God leaves him to the spirit of evil which he accepted of his own free choice, delivers him to it, and so he practices his evil, which rebounds upon him.

37.5.s.en: 3. The king of Assyria reproaches the Lord:

37.5.0.en: 8 So Rabshakeh returned, and found the king of Assyria warring against Libnah: for he had heard that he was departed from Lachish. 9 And he heard say concerning Tirhakah king of Cush, "He is come forth to make war with thee." And when he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying, 10 "Thus shall ye speak to Hezekiah king of Judah, saying, Let not thy God, in whom thou trustest, deceive thee, saying, Jerusalem shall not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria. 11 Behold, thou hast heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands by destroying them utterly; and shalt thou be delivered? 12 Have the gods of the nations delivered them which my fathers have destroyed, as Gozan, and Haran, and Rezeph, and the children of Eden which were in Telassar? 13 Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arphad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah?"

37.5.1.en: Rabshakeh returned to Sennacherib to find that he had left Lachish and gone to Libnah to fight against it.

37.5.2.en: "Libnah" is a name meaning "whiteness," a city between Lachish and Makkedah (Josh 10:39; 12:15), in the portion of Judah, assigned to the sons of Aaron (Josh 21:13). It is thought likely to be at the place called Tell Burnat, at a distance of two miles northwest of Beit Jibrin, and it is supposed to be Tell es-Safi or es-Safiya.

37.6.0.en: The king heard that Tirhakah king of Egypt and Cush [9] had come out to fight him, so he sent to Hezekiah once more, threatening him, demanding the submission of Jerusalem and its surrender to him, blaspheming God, on whom Hezekiah relies.

37.6.1.en: Some ask why Sennacherib repeated his threat. Perhaps because he was surrounded by hostile nations and feared Tirhakah, the strong king of Egypt and Cush, so he wanted to take Jerusalem without bloodshed to be a support for him.

37.6.2.en: Despite the blasphemy against God that the message carried, it is shorter than the first and much milder in its tone, perhaps because he wanted to win Hezekiah and persuade him without provoking him. He showed him that there is no personal enmity against him, but that it is a battle between the god of Sennacherib, who has overcome all the gods of the other nations, and the God of Hezekiah...

37.6.3.en: Our spiritual battle is in truth a battle between God and the devil; we are not a party to it, and cannot be a party. If we hide in God we gain the victory by Him and in Him, however much the enemy tries to reproach us! This is what the prophet David realized when he saw Goliath the giant opposing his people, for he said: "For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?" (1 Sam 17:26), "Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts..." (1 Sam 17:45).

37.7.0.en: 14 And Hezekiah received the letters from the hand of the messengers, and read them: and Hezekiah went up unto the house of the LORD, and spread them before the LORD. 15 And Hezekiah prayed unto the LORD, saying, 16 "O LORD of hosts, God of Israel, that sittest above the cherubims, thou art the God, even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth: thou hast made heaven and earth. 17 Incline thine ear, O LORD, and hear; open thine eyes, O LORD, and see: and hear all the words of Sennacherib, which he hath sent to reproach the living God. 18 Of a truth, LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste all the nations, and their countries, 19 And have cast their gods into the fire: for they were no gods, but the work of men's hands, wood and stone: therefore they have destroyed them. 20 Now therefore, O LORD our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that thou art the LORD, even thou only."

37.7.1.en: Hezekiah took Sennacherib's written letter from the hand of the messengers and read it, then went up to the house of the LORD and spread it before the LORD, then prayed [14-15].

37.7.2.en: If Sennacherib reckoned that he bore no personal enmity toward Hezekiah but that it was a battle between gods, Hezekiah set out to his God to lay the matter before Him in His holy house. Perhaps among the most beautiful traits of Hezekiah is that he was a man of prayer, for on five occasions we hear of him that he enjoys power through prayer.

37.7.3.en: The following is observed in his prayer:

37.7.4.en: a. The openness of his heart in prayer together with his reverence and humility... He did not justify himself in anything, but disappeared completely, setting the matter in full frankness in God's hands.

37.7.5.en: b. He calls God "LORD of hosts," as the mighty Commander of the battle, whose hosts are heavenly, able to give victory and triumph over the enemy.

37.7.6.en: St. Jerome tells us of an Egyptian monk called Abba Aban: [One of those working in the fields beside the river asked him to drive away from them the "Behemoth" (a kind of Egyptian crocodile), which was harming them by its violence, and he, in a gentle voice, commanded the animal: "I adjure you in the name of Jesus Christ to depart," and the animal began to withdraw as though by an angel, and no longer appeared in that region].

37.7.7.en: In Christ Jesus our Lord we enjoy sure victory. Origen asked: [If Satan and his powers have truly been crushed, how do we believe that he still has such authority against the servants of God? And he answers, saying: The violent activity of Satan has its effect on the wicked alone, but he no longer has authority over those who are in Christ.

37.7.8.en: c. He calls God the One who sits above the cherubim, for He has no need of a temporal throne, but His throne is heavenly... Therefore in His work He seeks not what is for Himself but what is for the edification of His people and His believers.

37.7.9.en: d. He calls God "God of all the kingdoms of the earth," and not only the God of Israel; all the nations are in His hand, and He moves the whole world by His holy will.

37.7.10.en: e. Truly Sennacherib overcame the neighboring nations and cast their gods into the fire to burn and perish... but what can he do to the Creator?!

37.8.0.en: f. He offered a wonderful conclusion to the prayer: "Now therefore, O LORD our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that thou art the LORD, even thou only" [20]. It is as though the victory You give us is a witness in the world to the sincerity of our faith in You, and that You, You alone are God, and there is no other besides You.

37.9.0.en: 21 Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent unto Hezekiah, saying, "Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Whereas thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria: 22 This is the word which the LORD hath spoken concerning him; She hath despised thee, and laughed thee to scorn, the virgin, the daughter of Zion; the daughter of Jerusalem hath shaken her head at thee. 23 Whom hast thou reproached and blasphemed? and against whom hast thou exalted thy voice, and lifted up thine eyes on high? even against the Holy One of Israel. 24 By the hand of thy servants hast thou reproached the Lord, and hast said, By the multitude of my chariots am I come up to the height of the mountains, to the sides of Lebanon; and I will cut down the tall cedars thereof, and the choice fir trees thereof: and I will enter into the height of his border, the forest of his Carmel. 25 I have digged, and drunk water; and with the sole of my feet will I dry up all the streams of Egypt. 26 Hast thou not heard long ago, how I have done it; and of ancient times, that I have formed it? Now have I brought it to pass, that thou shouldest be to lay waste defenced cities into ruinous heaps. 27 Therefore their inhabitants were of small power, they were dismayed and confounded: they were as the grass of the field, and as the green herb, as the grass on the housetops, and as corn blasted before it be grown up. 28 But I know thy abode, and thy going out, and thy coming in, and thy rage against me. 29 Because thy rage against me, and thy pride, is come up into mine ears, therefore will I put my hook in thy nose, and my bridle in thy lips, and I will turn thee back by the way by which thou camest. 30 And this shall be a sign unto thee: Ye shall eat this year such as groweth of itself; and the second year that which springeth of the same; and in the third year sow ye, and reap, and plant vineyards, and eat the fruit thereof. 31 And the remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah shall again take root downward, and bear fruit upward. 32 For out of Jerusalem shall go forth a remnant, and they that escape out of mount Zion: the zeal of the LORD of hosts shall do this. 33 Therefore thus saith the LORD concerning the king of Assyria, He shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with shields, nor cast a bank against it. 34 By the way that he came, by the same shall he return, and shall not come into this city, saith the LORD. 35 For I will defend this city to save it for mine own sake, and for my servant David's sake."

37.9.1.en: Hezekiah prayed to God, and the answer came quickly by way of Isaiah the prophet, the content of which is as follows:

37.10.0.en: a. If Sennacherib blasphemed God and mocked Him, the Lord directed His speech to Sennacherib, mocking him, saying: "She hath despised thee, the daughter of Zion hath laughed thee to scorn; the daughter of Jerusalem hath shaken her head at thee..." [22] and so on... It is as though He were saying to him: If you have raged against Me like a ravenous beast, I know how to restrain you and mock you through the virgin, the daughter of Zion, the daughter of Jerusalem... or as though He were saying to him: You come to Me with your massive army, and I crush you by a virgin girl who despises you. You boast of the multitude of your chariots, for you went up to the high mountains and cut down the cedars of Lebanon and its fir trees and went deep into the wild thicket of Carmel, and you did not perceive My power, for when I dig in the mountains with My hand I send forth water to drink, and when I tread the rivers with My feet I dry them up; in My hand are the keys of nature... Remember what I did to Pharaoh in the days of the prophet Moses [24-26]. Remember what I did to the nations when I gave the Promised Land to My people! Learn from history through practical events so that you may not be crushed!

37.10.1.en: God declares to Sennacherib that He is the Controller of all and the Knower of secrets, and He has no need for him to send letters blaspheming Him, for He knows his sitting down and his going out and his coming in and his raging against Him... and He is able to bridle him like animals, putting a hook in his nose and a bridle in his lips, and to turn him about like a led animal to return from where he came.

37.10.2.en: In other words, God mocked him in several ways: He can humiliate him through a virgin girl who despises him; He stirs up nature against him, controls his movements and leads him where he does not wish! In other words, God humbles the enemy of good through His virgin, chaste Church, making nature serve on behalf of His queen, and crushing all the resources and plans of the enemy of good.

37.10.3.en: It is told in the life of St. Melania that the enemy of good realized that all his struggles against her had failed; he felt defeated and surrendered, and was no longer able to resist her. And Origen sees that it is fitting for us to blame ourselves when we sin, and not to reckon that Satan is the cause of our error, as the simple common people think. We have been given in Christ Jesus the power to crush the enemy if we wish.

37.11.0.en: b. God gave Hezekiah a glorious sign to remove from him the terror of the hardships that came upon him because of Sennacherib's invasion [30-32]. If the enemy had seized the harvest so that no seed remained for sowing, which leads to the occurrence of famine or at least to a shortage of food, then the crop comes up that year without need of seed (perhaps from the remnants that fell by chance); and so in the following year, and in the third year, when the people recover their strength, life returns to normal. It is as though God works wonders for them as long as they are helpless and their resources are exhausted, until, when they are in their normal state, He works by them through the natural life and through the laws of nature.

37.12.0.en: This sign was a symbol of the remnant that escaped from Judah, for their deliverance is a gift from God despite the resistance and violence of the enemies, as He says: "They shall again take root downward, and bear fruit upward" [31], as though the enemy had uprooted them completely, so that they became like those without roots, but God raises them up and gives them fruit, as He did with the crop in the first and second years of Sennacherib's invasion... "The zeal of the LORD of hosts shall do this" [32]. That is, this salvation is not accomplished by human merit but out of God's love for His people and His jealousy over them, being the heavenly Bridegroom jealous over His bride, that she may be holy to Him and that no other may seize her.

37.12.1.en: "Thus saith the LORD of hosts; I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great jealousy" (Zech 1:14).

37.12.2.en: "For the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God" (Ex 34:14).

37.12.3.en: Through this sign God declares blessings toward His people, which are:

37.12.4.en: First: the deliverance of the people from judgment, so that famine does not come upon them but they enjoy abundant fruit [30].

37.13.0.en: Second: the remnant is planted anew in Jerusalem [32], a reference to the renewal of human nature and God's care for His Church.

37.13.1.en: Third: they bear fruit upward [31], that is, they carry a heavenly, exalted nature.

37.13.2.en: Fourth: the spread of the preaching from Jerusalem [32].

37.13.3.en: Fifth: the secret of this saving work is the fire of God's love and His burning zeal [32].

37.14.0.en: c. God's assurance that Sennacherib will not enter Jerusalem [33-35]; he will not shoot one arrow toward it nor come before it with a shield, nor cast a bank against it... but will return in shame to where he came from. So God, in His love for His children, uses every means to remove anxiety from them, assuring them of His protection, His care and His practical love toward them.

37.15.0.en: d. The secret of His protection of His people is not their own righteousness but His jealousy for His glory and for His covenants with His beloved children such as David. It is not for the sake of Judah, nor for the sake of Hezekiah's moving prayers, that God intervenes, but as He said: "For I will defend this city to save it for mine own sake, and for my servant David's sake" [35].

37.15.1.en: David died, but his life continues through his lifted-up prayers, for the sake of which God defends the city of Jerusalem.

37.16.s.en: 6. The smiting of the Assyrian army:

37.16.0.en: "Then the angel of the LORD went forth, and smote of the army of Assyria a hundred and fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses." [36].

37.16.1.en: By the angel of the LORD is most often meant the Word of God before the Incarnation, and this was fulfilled on the very night that followed the prophet Isaiah's talk with Hezekiah (2 Kgs 19:35).

37.16.2.en: Sennacherib was defeated this time although he had previously besieged Hezekiah and humiliated him, for in one of the excavations found in the ruins of Nineveh there are words on the tongue of Sennacherib that he attacked Hezekiah and took 46 horses and small cities, and also carried captive 150 and 200 persons, great and small, male and female, and a great number of animals; and that he shut up Hezekiah in Jerusalem like a bird in a cage and set up ramparts before his city and imposed on him a doubled tribute, etc...

37.17.s.en: 7. The death of Sennacherib and his son Sharezer:

37.17.0.en: 37 So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh. 38 And it came to pass, as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons smote him with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Ararat: and Esarhaddon his son reigned in his stead.

37.17.1.en: Sennacherib was killed, and his son with him, while he was bowing down in the house of Nisroch his god, whom he thought able to protect him and the secret of his victory over all the nations and their gods...
